page: Microsoft Azure E64ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running up to 3.7 GHz. Configured with 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading, the instance provides 512 GB of system memory, matching an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. CPU extensions include AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support), VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic instructions, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster.

Local ephemeral capacity is delivered via an integrated 3,780 GB NVMe solid-state drive, eliminating dependency on network-attached volumes for high-throughput scratch data. The server contains no discrete GPUs. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates upper-quartile compute capability, scoring 22,274.0 on Geekbench multi-core, which ranks in the top ten percent of tested machines. Cached memory bandwidth tops 4,863.62 GB/sec, while uncached large-block write bandwidth reaches 108.83 GB/sec.

System benchmarks reflect significant operational density for memory-bound tasks. The instance delivers 89.03 million operations per second in Redis SET testing and achieves 29,401.17 in PassMark database execution. Multi-threaded decompression through bzip3 yields 359.69 GB/sec. On CPU-driven language model inference, it generates 4,658.62 tokens per second for prompt processing on lightweight 135M parameter models, though throughput scales down to 16.6 tokens per second when executing 70B parameter models without hardware accelerators.

By consolidating 512 GB of RAM with nearly 3.8 TB of directly attached NVMe storage, the E64ads_v6 yields balanced operational efficiency for stateful memory platforms. It avoids external storage network latency and bandwidth costs for transient data, making it suitable for large in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, heavy relational database servers, and multi-threaded data engineering pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E64ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor offering 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores clocked up to 3.7 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 vector extensions, it features 512 GB of system memory at an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and includes a bundled 3,780 GB NVMe SSD for fast local storage without discrete GPUs. In empirical tests, the instance records a Geekbench multi-core score of 22,274.0, 89.03 million Redis SET operations per second, and 359.69 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The combination of dense memory allocation, top-quartile CPU throughput, and high-capacity local NVMe storage delivers high operational efficiency for memory-intensive workloads, including large relational database engines, Redis and Memcached clusters, data analytics engines, and enterprise ETL pipelines.
